replication.target_description: Central replication: GSS 2012, 2014, 2016, and 2018; two-sample, two-tailed t-test comparing post-secularists with traditionalists on the evolution question. The report explicitly identifies years not used in the original study as the central replication point.

n.sample_role: Target test observations are respondents in the traditional and post-secular classes. The reported 2,269 observations describe the replication sample; the latent-class analysis also identifies a modern class. Final counts for the two comparison groups are not supplied.
n.exclusions: Target-test exclusions and final comparison-group counts not reported.
n.location: PDF-text page 3, Years Following the Original Sample
n.quote:
The replication using years 2012, 2014, 2016, and 2018 included 2,269 observations, which met
the stage 1 threshold of 153 observations defined by the power analysis.

es.location: PDF-text page 3, Years Following the Original Sample
es.quote:
secularists (mean =.04, std. error = .01) have significantly (t-statistic = 16.57, degrees of freedom
= 1,436, p = .0000 by Stata16) different rates of correct responses, compared to traditionalists
(mean = .41, std. error = .02).

notes:
Identity assessment: supplied cache identifies OSF download h7jfv and the exact supplied project title. Primary Final Report, Replication of a Research Claim from O’Brien & Noy (2015), from American Sociological Review, credited to Marco Ramljak and Erick Axxe, dated October 22, 2020. Its original-study reference and DOI match the input. The input reference date November 18, 2025 differs from the internal report date; no network verification performed. Text contains claim, results, methods, deviations, and references, rather than an abstract-only excerpt. No PDF supplied. Three analyses are presented: all years, original years, and subsequent years. Target selection follows the explicit central-replication statement, not row order or numeric matching: The central replication point reflects the years not
used in the original study. The subsequent-years narrative states: The replication yielded a negative Cohen’s d in the focal test
(90%), corresponding to an effect in the same pattern compared to the original study. Its percentage-form d description does not establish an unambiguous conventional numeric d; do not interpret 90% as d = -0.90. Retained the printed t statistic with its actual metric, without conversion. Analytic N unresolved: 2,269 is not established as the two-class test N, no final mutually exclusive comparison-group counts printed, and no N inferred from df. No arithmetic derivation performed. Original side, replication p, and reported_success are unassigned placeholders only.
